title: Palestinians Want a Two-State Solution
gist: Arab Barometer researchers Robbins, Jamal and Tessler note that a year after Trump's September 2025 Gaza peace plan, it has stalled — Hamas has not disarmed, Israel controls over 60% of the strip and reconstruction has barely begun — while arguing that a new Palestinian majority, even in Gaza, supports compromise with Israel. Only the article's opening is available (teaser).

insights.claim: A year after Trump unveiled his September 2025 Gaza peace plan, it has stalled: Hamas has not disarmed, Israel still controls more than 60% of the strip, and the promised technocratic government and international security force have not materialized.
insights.speaker: Michael Robbins
insights.so_what: The absence of a functioning post-war framework sustains Middle East geopolitical risk premia and delays any reconstruction-driven investment.
insights.quote: Israel still controls more than 60 percent of the strip

insights.claim: Large-scale reconstruction in Gaza has barely begun, and most Gazans still struggle to obtain food, water and shelter.
insights.speaker: Michael Robbins
insights.so_what: Humanitarian conditions remain a source of regional instability and diplomatic pressure on Israel.

insights.claim: Ahead of Israel's October election, Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has hardened his position, further complicating the peace process.
insights.speaker: Michael Robbins
insights.so_what: Israeli electoral politics are a near-term catalyst for the direction of Gaza policy.
insights.locator: And as Israel’s October election approaches

insights.claim: Survey researchers from Arab Barometer argue a new majority of Palestinians — even in Gaza — supports compromise with Israel via a two-state solution.
insights.speaker: Michael Robbins
insights.so_what: If accurate, public opinion is less of a barrier to a negotiated settlement than often assumed, shifting the bottleneck to leadership and politics.
insights.quote: Why a New Majority—Even in Gaza—Supports Compromise With Israel
